assessments.reasoning: gpl_reciprocal [29011,29514) is the clause in the 29 June 2007 GPLv3 edition. It expressly names AGPL version 3, retains GPL terms on its covered part, and applies the referenced network requirements to the combination as such. Independent co-deployment, a §5 aggregate, or substitution of GPLv2-only code does not establish this route.

agpl_terms [28300,28957) supplies the requirements imported by GPLv3. For a licensee's modified version supporting remote interaction, all interacting remote users must receive a prominent opportunity to obtain that version's Corresponding Source free from a network server through customary or standard copying means. It includes Corresponding Source for GPLv3 material incorporated by the specified route. An unmodified deployment alone or an offer of another version's archive cannot establish satisfaction of the claimed trigger and duty.

challenge.method: Tested three readings against both originals: retaining GPLv3 exempts the GPL part's source, the counterpart relicenses the whole work, or forming a combination automatically requires an offer to everyone.
challenge.results: The retained GPL terms coexist with the combination-wide network rule and the AGPL sentence including incorporated GPLv3 Corresponding Source. The counterpart imports the special network requirements without imposing every AGPL term on the GPL part. Forming the combination alone does not establish the modification, supported remote interaction, or audience required for the offer.

limitations: This conclusion concerns the two named editions and their single-work route. The texts alone establish neither combined-work status nor an actual modification or remote interaction.
reasoning: GPLv3 §13 permits forming and conveying one combined work with an AGPLv3-licensed work. GPLv3 remains on the GPL-covered part. AGPLv3 remains on its part under its own §13. The GPL counterpart expressly applies AGPLv3 §13's special network requirements to the combination as such, with their original conditions.
